title: S&P DJI December quarterly rebalance — the constituent announcement (S&P 500/100/400/600), after the close
source: EST: date derived from S&P Dow Jones Indices' own published announcements and verified mechanically against them, 2026-09-08. THE EVIDENCE IS NO LONGER A RULE-QUOTE PLUS ONE YEAR OF PRECEDENT: this session fetched S&P DJI's own newsroom index direct (press.spglobal.com/index.php?s=2429&l=100 plus offsets o=100..800, nine requests, all HTTP 200, ~117KB each) and reconstructed the complete release archive — 899 unique dated releases spanning 2022-05-06 to 2026-09-04. Of the 18 quarterly rebalance cycles inside that window, 17 produced a constituent announcement, and ALL 17 landed on exactly the first Friday two weeks before that month's third Friday, checked by weekday arithmetic computed in-session: 2022-06-03, 2022-09-02, 2022-12-02, 2023-03-03, 2023-06-02, 2023-09-01, 2023-12-01, 2024-03-01, 2024-06-07, 2024-09-06, 2024-12-06, 2025-03-07, 2025-09-05, 2025-12-05, 2026-03-06, 2026-06-05, 2026-09-04. December alone is 4 for 4 (2022-12-02, 2023-12-01, 2024-12-06, 2025-12-05). THE ARITHMETIC FOR THIS INSTANCE: December 2026's Fridays are the 4th, 11th, 18th and 25th, so the third Friday is 2026-12-18 (tracked here as opex-2026-12-18 on a confirmed OCC prefix), the effective open is Monday 2026-12-21, and the first Friday two weeks prior is 2026-12-04. THE ONE MEASURED EXCEPTION IS NOT A DATE MISS BUT AN ABSENCE: the June 2025 cycle produced no constituent announcement at all — the archive carries no rebalance release on or near 2025-06-06 — so roughly 1 cycle in 18 is a no-op, which is a real risk to this entry and is recorded rather than smoothed over. Filed estimate on three counts, none of which is date doubt: no S&P DJI document published for December 2026 exists yet (this is a forward derivation, not a reading), the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no member for an index owner's own published schedule, and a lane may not self-confirm an event it derived. The owner's document library (spglobal.com/spdji/en/documents/index-news-and-announcements/) and its US-indices methodology PDF both returned 403 to this runner and are recorded in the ledger's probe-ref.blocked rather than silently substituted. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: WHY THE ANNOUNCEMENT AND NOT THE EFFECTIVE DATE. Proposed by the sp-quarterly-rebalance-effective-2026-09-21 initial research (2026-09-08), which measured the S&P quarterly rebalance and found the effect sits at the announcement, not at the effective open: at index level the effective open is a null (SPY, Monday after the third Friday, 2005-2026: 40 of 83 negative, sign p=82.6%, no relative-volume step), while the announcement-reaction session moved 28 of 32 named companies in the direction their index action predicts. THE INITIAL RESEARCH ON THIS ENTRY TESTED THAT FINDING OUT OF SAMPLE AND SPLIT IT IN TWO. Parsing all 17 archived quarterly releases yielded 700 constituent rows (Effective Date / Index / Action / Company / Ticker / GICS), and 549 of them were measurable close-to-close against their own tier's ETF from api.nasdaq.com daily bars — 16 cycles sharing zero observations with the sibling's single intraday cross-section. CONFIRMED: S&P SmallCap 600 additions n=163, +3.12% mean excess vs IJR, 122/163 correctly signed, sign p<0.001%; deletions n=146, -3.10%, 118/146, p<0.001%. REFUTED: the sibling's 'the index effect is dead in the S&P 500' rests on n=3; on n=35 the S&P 500 addition cohort is the STRONGEST tier, +5.22% mean, 27/35, p=0.188%, on the highest relative turnover of any tier (3.67x). ALSO REFUTED: the reversal hypothesis — the 600 cohort's pop does not give back, with median drift from the reaction close to the effective Monday of -0.38% (83/163 negative, p=87.6%, an honest null) and only 43 of 122 positive names surrendering half their excess. WHAT IS ACTUALLY DECAYING: split at the panel midpoint, 600 additions ran +4.43% at 59/66 (89%) in 2022-06..2024-03 and +2.23% at 63/97 (65%) in 2024-06..2026-06 — Mann-Whitney p=0.06%, two-proportion p=0.04%. The December tilt the proposal suspected is real in direction and NOT significant: 18/29 (62%) vs 104/134 (78%), Mann-Whitney p=13.0%, two-proportion p=8.0%, and December relative turnover is normal (1.91x vs 1.70x, p=25.5%) — flow arrives, price moves less, but not distinguishably so. TWO SIBLING MILESTONES REMAIN DELIBERATELY UNFILED, and this session did not re-litigate them: the capped/alternatively-weighted pro-forma (2026-12-11) and the December effective open (2026-12-21). The sibling declined both on an index-level SPY null this research did not re-measure; the constituent-level persistence above is not evidence against that null, because it is a different unit of observation. What would reopen them is named in the ledger. Impact low, symbols deliberately empty: the flow lives in individual names unknowable three months out, and an ETF proxy would only make the deterministic screen trip on broad-market beta. Kind 'sector' matches the sibling market-structure flow entries; the enum has no index-flow member and the imperfect fit is named rather than fixed from this lane. See docs/research/events/sp-rebalance-proforma-2026-12-04.md.
